chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, who said:
Indeed the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Kill the polytheists, but spare their elders and their children.'

key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِينَ: Polytheists (those who associate partners with God)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about killing polytheists and sparing their families?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter detailing the methodology of warfare, this hadith establishes a key principle of selective engagement during military campaigns. It distinguishes between combatants and non-combatants, instructing Muslims to kill polytheists who are actively fighting while sparing their elders and children, reflecting the Shia scholarly understanding of proportional conduct in battle. This narration serves as a foundational text for understanding the rules of engagement in early Islamic history.
